Hi Alice —

Thanks for the patience. Please find the requested artifacts attached and a short summary below. (I can send a single consolidated PDF if you prefer.)

Summary: 
- Retention matrix: session snapshots are classified as 'ephemeral debug artifacts' with a default tenant-scoped retention of 30 days. Customers can request an extended short-term preserve for investigative purposes; preserves are granted in 30/90-day increments and require a customer-signed hold approval (DocuSign).

- Conditional erase: when a tenant requests deletion, we run a two-stage removal: (1) immediate logical removal from search/indexing and tenant-visible UI components; (2) scheduled secure purge from storage backend and KV caches within 7–30 days depending on shard replication windows. Forensic artifacts (if required by legal/regulatory exception) are isolated into an escrowed snapshot and retained only under a documented carveout with an expiration. All deletions are recorded in our deletion audit log and hash-based verification records are generated.

- Exceptions/carveouts: We offer a timeboxed carveout process for customers who need temporary preservation. The carveout requires: (a) a documented justification, (b) customer-signed approval (DocuSign), and (c) an internal approval by Security + Legal. Carveouts are visually flagged in our retention dashboard and automatically expire per the requested window unless renewed.

Attachments included (redacted where applicable):
1) redwood-retention-matrix_v1.xlsx — retention buckets and tenant override flow
2) sig-caiq-extract-20270506.pdf — SIG/CAIQ mappings relevant to artifact retention and deletion controls
3) proof-of-delete-playbook.pdf — example evidence packet showing removal steps, audit log excerpts, and hash verification sample

Next steps:

- If you want the low-level kernel debug traces included in evidence, we need written approval and a scoped request; those are treated as high-sensitivity artifacts and require an elevated retention justification.
